001.Black_footed_Albatross.description: A small, dark albatross seen primarily in the North Pacific. It nests on remote islands and spends most of its life at sea.

002.Laysan_Albatross.description: A small albatross with a white head and body and dark upper wings. Known for its graceful flight and long lifespan.

003.Sooty_Albatross.description: A medium-sized albatross with sooty-brown plumage and a diamond-shaped tail. It breeds on sub-Antarctic islands.

004.Groove_billed_Ani.description: A tropical black bird in the cuckoo family, known for its large, grooved bill and communal breeding habits.

005.Crested_Auklet.description: A small seabird of the North Pacific, famous for its forward-curving crest and tangerine-scented plumage during breeding season.

006.Least_Auklet.description: The smallest species of auklet. They nest in large colonies in rocky crevices on islands in the Bering Sea.

007.Parakeet_Auklet.habitat: North Pacific cliffs and rocky slopes
007.Parakeet_Auklet.description: A small seabird with a distinctive circular red bill. It nests in crevices on cliffs and slopes.

008.Rhinoceros_Auklet.habitat: North Pacific Ocean, burrows on islands
008.Rhinoceros_Auklet.description: Named for the horn-like extension on its bill during breeding season. A close relative of puffins, it nests in burrows.

009.Brewer_Blackbird.description: A medium-sized blackbird common in the West. Males are glossy black with a purple sheen on the head; females are brownish-grey.

010.Red_winged_Blackbird.description: One of the most abundant birds across North America. Males are black with bright red and yellow shoulder patches.

011.Rusty_Blackbird.description: Breeds in the boreal forests of Canada and Alaska. Populations have declined steeply. Named for rusty edges on winter plumage.

012.Yellow_headed_Blackbird.description: Males are striking with a bright yellow head and chest against a black body. They inhabit freshwater marshes in the West.

013.Bobolink.description: A bird of the grasslands, known for the male's bubbling song and 'tuxedo-backward' plumage pattern. Migrates long distances to South America.

014.Indigo_Bunting.description: Males are a brilliant indigo blue all over. They frequent weedy fields and shrubby areas in the Eastern US.

015.Lazuli_Bunting.description: The western counterpart to the Indigo Bunting. Males have a turquoise head/back, rusty breast, and white belly.

016.Painted_Bunting.description: Males are arguably the most colorful bird in North America, with a blue head, red underparts, and green back.

017.Cardinal.description: A familiar backyard bird. Males are brilliant red with a black mask and crest; females are brownish with red accents.

018.Spotted_Catbird.description: A bowerbird species with emerald green plumage and white spotting. Known for its unique cat-like wailing calls.

019.Gray_Catbird.description: A slate-gray bird with a black cap and chestnut undertail. Famous for its meowing call and mimicry abilities.

020.Yellow_breasted_Chat.description: A large, elusive bird with a bright yellow breast and spectacles. Known for its bizarre series of clicks, whistles, and hoots.

021.Eastern_Towhee.description: A large sparrow of the Eastern scrub. Males are black, white, and rust-colored. Known for their 'drink-your-tea' song.

022.Chuck_will_Widow.description: The largest nightjar in North America. Camouflaged like dead leaves, it hunts insects at night and is named after its call.

023.Brandt_Cormorant.description: A seabird of the Pacific coast. Breeding adults have a bright blue throat pouch. They dive deep for fish.

024.Red_faced_Cormorant.description: Range restricted to the North Pacific. Named for the bare red skin on its face. Nests on steep cliffs.

025.Pelagic_Cormorant.description: Small and slender cormorant. Despite its name, it stays close to rocky shores. Glossy black with white flank patches in breeding season.

026.Bronzed_Cowbird.description: A brood parasite that lays eggs in other birds' nests. Males have a red eye and a glossy, bronzed ruff on the neck.

027.Shiny_Cowbird.description: A recent arrival to North America from the south. Males are glossy violet-black; females are plain brown. Brood parasite.

028.Brown_Creeper.description: A tiny woodland bird that spirals up tree trunks searching for insects. Cryptically patterned to match tree bark.

029.American_Crow.description: A large, intelligent all-black bird. Highly social and adaptable, found in nearly every habitat across North America.

030.Fish_Crow.description: Similar to American Crow but smaller and with a nasal call. Primarily found along the East and Gulf Coasts.

031.Black_billed_Cuckoo.description: Slender and secretive bird. Unlike European cuckoos, they usually raise their own young. Voracious eaters of caterpillars.

032.Mangrove_Cuckoo.description: A shy bird of Florida's mangroves. distinguished by its buffy underparts and black mask.

033.Yellow_billed_Cuckoo.description: Known as the 'Rain Crow' for its calling before storms. Identify by the yellow lower bill and large white tail spots.

034.Gray_crowned_Rosy_Finch.description: A rugged finch of high mountains and islands. Brown body with pink on wings/belly and a gray head patch.

035.Purple_Finch.description: Males are raspberry red (described as dipped in cranberry juice). A chunky forest finch with a heavy beak.

036.Northern_Flicker.description: A large, brownish woodpecker that often feeds on the ground (ants). Flashy yellow or red underwings in flight.

037.Acadian_Flycatcher.description: A greenish 'empu' flycatcher of the Eastern forests. Best identified by its explosive 'PEET-sah' song.

038.Great_Crested_Flycatcher.description: A large flycatcher with a yellow belly and cinnamon tail. Nests in cavities and often uses snakeskin in nests.

039.Least_Flycatcher.description: One of the smallest flycatchers. Identified by its dry 'che-beck' call. Common in open deciduous forests.

040.Olive_sided_Flycatcher.description: Perches on high, dead branches. Dark 'vest' appearance. Distinctive song sounds like 'Quick, three beers!'.

041.Scissor_tailed_Flycatcher.description: Unmistakable with its extremely long, forked tail. It perches on fences and wires, catching insects in midair.

042.Vermilion_Flycatcher.description: Males are a brilliant, eye-catching red with a dark mask. They are often seen flycatching from low perches.

043.Yellow_bellied_Flycatcher.description: A small, active flycatcher of the northern bogs. Yellowish underparts and throat. Hard to see in dense vegetation.

044.Frigatebird.description: A large seabird with a long forked tail and angular wings. Males have a red throat pouch they inflate to attract mates.

045.Northern_Fulmar.habitat: Open North Atlantic and North Pacific
045.Northern_Fulmar.description: Looks like a gull but is related to petrels (has a tube nose). Common in cold northern oceans, often following ships.

046.Gadwall.description: A subtly patterned duck. Males are gray-brown with a black rear end. Often overlooked among mallards.

047.American_Goldfinch.description: The bright yellow 'wild canary'. Males are yellow with black cap/wings. They love thistle seeds.

048.European_Goldfinch.description: Distinctive red face and black/white head pattern. Golden wing bars are visible in flight.

049.Boat_tailed_Grackle.description: A large, lanky blackbird with a long, keel-shaped tail. Males are glossy black; females are brown.

050.Eared_Grebe.description: Small grebe with golden ear tufts in breeding plumage. Nests in colonies on floating vegetation.

051.Horned_Grebe.description: Striking breeding plumage with golden 'horns' behind the eyes. Winter plumage is stark black and white.

052.Pied_billed_Grebe.description: Small, brownish grebe with a thick, chicken-like bill. Expert at sinking slowly into the water to hide.

053.Western_Grebe.description: Elegant, long-necked grebe with black and white plumage. Famous for their 'rushing' courtship ceremony across water.

054.Blue_Grosbeak.description: Large, deep blue bird with chestnut wing bars and a heavy silver bill. Often flicks its tail sideways.

055.Evening_Grosbeak.description: A bulky finch with a massive bill. Males are yellow, black, and white. Their populations are irruptive and declining.

056.Pine_Grosbeak.description: Large, sluggish finch. Males are pinkish-red; females are gray with yellow head/rump. Tame and approachable.

057.Rose_breasted_Grosbeak.description: Males are black and white with a brilliant red triangle on the breast. Known for their lovely, robin-like song.

058.Pigeon_Guillemot.description: A dark seabird with a white wing patch and bright red legs/mouth. Nests in rocky crevices near the water.

059.California_Gull.description: The gull that saved the Mormon crops from crickets. Medium-sized with dark eyes and yellow legs.

060.Glaucous_winged_Gull.description: A large, pale-gray gull. The wingtips are the same color as the mantle (gray), not black.

061.Heermann_Gull.description: Distinctive gull of the California coast with a gray body, black tail, and red bill. Often harasses pelicans for food.

062.Herring_Gull.description: The quintessential 'seagull'. Large, with pink legs and a red spot on the lower mandible. Widespread and adaptable.

063.Ivory_Gull.description: A pure white gull of the high Arctic. It follows polar bears to scavenge on seal kills.

064.Ring_billed_Gull.description: A medium-sized gull with a yellow bill encircled by a black ring. Very common inland and often near people.

065.Slaty_backed_Gull.description: A large, dark-backed gull from Asia that occasionally visits Alaska and the West Coast.

066.Western_Gull.description: A large, bulky gull with a dark gray back and pink legs. The most common coastal gull in California.

067.Anna_Hummingbird.description: Males have a glossy red-pink head and throat that can look black in low light. Common year-round on the West Coast.

068.Ruby_throated_Hummingbird.description: The only breeding hummingbird in eastern North America. Males have a brilliant ruby-red throat gorget.

069.Rufous_Hummingbird.description: A feisty, copper-colored hummingbird. Notorious for aggressively defending flower territories during migration.

070.Green_Violetear.description: A large, dark green hummingbird with violet ear-patches and a blue-green tail. A rare stray to the US.

071.Long_tailed_Jaeger.description: Smallest of the jaegers. Breeding adults have exceedingly long central tail streamers. They prey on lemmings.

072.Pomarine_Jaeger.description: Large and powerfully built jaeger. Central tail feathers are twisted and spoon-shaped. Kleptoparasite of other seabirds.

073.Blue_Jay.description: Loud and colorful bird of eastern backyards. Blue, white, and black plumage with a crest. Known to mimic hawks.

074.Florida_Jay.description: Found only in Florida. Blue and gray without a crest. They live in cooperative family groups.

075.Green_Jay.description: Unmistakable tropical jay with a green back, yellow underparts, and blue head. Noisy and social.

076.Dark_eyed_Junco.description: Common 'snowbirds'. Slate-gray with white outer tail feathers that flash in flight. Ground feeders.

077.Tropical_Kingbird.description: A large tyrant flycatcher with a gray head and yellow belly. Very vocal and aggressive towards intruders.

078.Gray_Kingbird.description: A massive-billed flycatcher of the Caribbean and Florida. Pale gray above, white below. Perches on wires.

079.Belted_Kingfisher.description: Stocky bird with a shaggy crest. Plunges headfirst into water to catch fish. Females have a rusty belly band.

080.Green_Kingfisher.description: Tiny kingfisher of the southern border. Dark green upperparts and white collar. Low, fast flight over water.

081.Pied_Kingfisher.description: Black and white kingfisher known for its ability to hover over water before diving. Not native to Americas.

082.Ringed_Kingfisher.description: Largest kingfisher in the New World. Blue-gray above with a rich chestnut belly. Noisy rattling call.

083.White_breasted_Kingfisher.description: Large kingfisher with huge red bill and chocolate-brown head. Hunts small animals on land as well as fish.

084.Red_legged_Kittiwake.description: Small gull with bright red legs and a short bill. Nests on ledges in the Pribilof Islands.

085.Horned_Lark.description: Ground-dwelling bird of open lands. Males have black 'horns' (feather tufts) and a yellow/black face mask.

086.Pacific_Loon.description: Elegant diver with a gray head and black throat patch in summer. Requires open water for takeoff.

087.Mallard.description: The most familiar duck. Males have an iridescent green head; females are mottled brown.

088.Western_Meadowlark.description: A bird of the open West with a bright yellow breast and black V. Melodious, flute-like song.

089.Hooded_Merganser.description: Small duck with a fan-shaped crest. Males have a striking black and white head pattern. Nests in tree cavities.

090.Red_breasted_Merganser.description: Shaggy-crested diving duck with a long, thin, serrated bill for catching fish. Winters on salt water.

091.Mockingbird.description: Famous songster that mimics other birds, alarms, and sounds. Gray with white wing patches flashing in flight.

092.Nighthawk.description: Active at dawn/dusk. Flies erratically to catch insects. distinctive white bar across long, pointed wings.

093.Clark_Nutcracker.description: A gray bird of the Rockies. Famous for burying thousands of pine seeds and remembering where they are.

094.White_breasted_Nuthatch.description: Active bird that climbs down tree trunks headfirst. Blue-gray back, white face, and black cap.

095.Baltimore_Oriole.description: Males are flame-orange and black. They weave hanging bag-like nests, often in elm trees.

096.Hooded_Oriole.description: A brilliant yellow-orange oriole. Often associated with palm trees, where they hang their nests from fronds.

097.Orchard_Oriole.description: The smallest North American oriole. Males are a deep chestnut-brick color (not orange) with black.

098.Scott_Oriole.description: A Lemon-yellow and black oriole of the desert Southwest. Often associated with yucca plants.

099.Ovenbird.description: A ground-walking warbler. Olive-green above, spotted below. Named for its covered nest resembling a dutch oven.

100.Brown_Pelican.description: Large seabird that plunge-dives for fish. Iconic pouch for scooping up water and prey.

101.White_Pelican.description: A huge white bird with black wingtips. Unlike brown pelicans, they scoop fish while swimming, often in coordinated groups.

102.Western_Wood_Pewee.description: A nondescript gray flycatcher. Best identified by its harsh, buzzing 'pee-ear' song. Sits upright on dead branches.

103.Sayornis.description: A flycatcher of the open West. Gray-brown back with a salmon-colored belly. Often nests on buildings.

104.American_Pipit.description: Sparrow-sized ground bird that bobs its tail constantly. Slender bill and white outer tail feathers.

105.Whip_poor_Will.description: Camouflaged night bird heard far more often than seen. Chants its name 'whip-poor-will' endlessly on summer nights.

106.Horned_Puffin.description: Sea parrot with a massive yellow and red bill. Named for the fleshy 'horn' above the eye during breeding season.

107.Common_Raven.description: The largest songbird. Massive size, shaggy throat feathers, and wedge-shaped tail distinguish it from crows.

108.White_necked_Raven.description: Similar to Common Raven but smaller. The white neck feathers are usually hidden except in strong wind or display.

109.American_Redstart.description: A warbler that acts like a flycatcher. Males are black with bright orange patches on wings and tail, which they flash.

110.Geococcyx.description: A large, terrestrial cuckoo famous for running down prey (lizards, snakes). Can run up to 20 mph.

111.Loggerhead_Shrike.description: The 'Butcherbird'. A songbird with raptor habits, it impales prey (insects, small birds) on thorns or barbed wire.

112.Great_Grey_Shrike.description: Slightly larger than Loggerhead Shrike. Winters in the northern US. Pale gray with a black mask.

113.Baird_Sparrow.description: A secretive grassland sparrow. Declining due to habitat loss. best identified by its ochre face and necklace of streaks.

114.Black_throated_Sparrow.description: Striking sparrow of the desert. Gray with a bold black throat and white face stripes.

115.Brewer_Sparrow.description: The 'sagebrush sparrow'. Small, sandy-gray sparrow. Its song is a long series of buzzes and trills.

116.Chipping_Sparrow.description: Common and tame. Bright rufous cap in summer with a black eye-line. Song is a mechanical dry trill.

117.Clay_colored_Sparrow.description: Pale sparrow with a buffy collar and distinct ear patch. Song is a rhythmic series of insect-like buzzes.

118.House_Sparrow.description: Ubiquitous city bird. Not a true sparrow (weaver finch). Males have a black bib; females are plain brown.

119.Field_Sparrow.description: Small sparrow with a pink bill and sweet expression. Song sounds like a ping-pong ball coming to rest.

120.Fox_Sparrow.description: Large, chunky sparrow. Scratch at leaf litter with both feet like a towhee. Plumage varies from red to gray.

121.Grasshopper_Sparrow.description: Flat-headed, short-tailed sparrow. Song is a thin buzz that sounds like a grasshopper.

122.Harris_Sparrow.description: Largest of the sparrows. Breeding adults have a black bib, face, and crown. Winters in Great Plains.

123.Henslow_Sparrow.description: Secretive sparrow with an olive-greenish head. Song is a very short, pathetic 't-slick'.

124.Le_Conte_Sparrow.description: Beautiful golden-orange sparrow. Very secretive, skulking in dense grass like a mouse.

125.Lincoln_Sparrow.description: Dainty sparrow with fine, crisp streaking on a buffy breast. Shy and hard to see well.

126.Nelson_Sharp_tailed_Sparrow.description: Bright orange-buff face and breast. Breeds in interior prairies and coastal marshes.

127.Savannah_Sparrow.description: Widespread grassland sparrow. Usually shows a yellow wash on the face near the eye.

128.Seaside_Sparrow.description: Dark, dingy sparrow restricted to salt marshes. Has a yellow spot before the eye.

129.Song_Sparrow.description: Highly variable but usually has coarse streaks converging into a central breast spot. Famous for its cheerful song.

130.Tree_Sparrow.description: Winter visitor to the US. Rufous cap and a dark central breast spot on a clear gray breast.

131.Vesper_Sparrow.description: Streaky sparrow with white outer tail feathers. Known for singing in the evening twilight.

132.White_crowned_Sparrow.description: Elegant sparrow with bold black and white head stripes. Young birds have brown and tan stripes.

133.White_throated_Sparrow.description: Well-defined white throat patch and yellow lores. Song is a clear whistle 'Oh-sweet-canada-canada'.

134.Cape_Glossy_Starling.description: A bird of southern Africa. Glossy blue-green plumage with a bright orange-yellow eye.

135.Bank_Swallow.description: Small swallow with brown back and a distinct brown breast band. Nests in burrows in sandy banks.

136.Barn_Swallow.description: Cobalt blue above, tawny below. Deeply forked tail. Nests in mud cups on man-made structures.

137.Cliff_Swallow.description: Square-tailed swallow with a buffy rump and chestnut throat. Builds gourd-shaped mud nests in colonies.

138.Tree_Swallow.description: Iridescent blue-green back and pure white underparts. Nests in tree cavities and bluebird boxes.

139.Scarlet_Tanager.description: Breeding males are blindingly red with jet-black wings and tail. They stay high in the canopy.

140.Summer_Tanager.description: The only entirely red bird in North America (males). Females are yellow. Specialized bee and wasp eaters.

141.Artic_Tern.description: The world's longest-distance migrant, flying pole to pole each year. White with a black cap and red beak.

142.Black_Tern.description: Small, graceful tern. Breeding adults are unmistakable with a black head and body and gray wings.

143.Caspian_Tern.description: The largest tern in the world. Heavy bright red bill and deep rasping call. Resembles a gull in bulk.

144.Common_Tern.description: Elegant seabird with a black cap, orange-red bill (with black tip), and deeply forked tail.

145.Elegant_Tern.description: A crowded nester on islands. Has a long, slender, slightly drooping orange bill and shaggy crest.

146.Forsters_Tern.description: Marsh-dwelling tern. In winter, it has a distinctive black eye patch (ear muffs) on a white head.

147.Least_Tern.description: The smallest North American tern. Distinctive yellow bill and white forehead patch. Nests on sandy flats.

148.Green_tailed_Towhee.description: A colorful sparrow relative with an olive-green back and rust-red cap. Secretive bird of mountain chaparral.

149.Brown_Thrasher.description: Large, foxy-red bird with a heavily streaked breast and long tail. Excellent mimic with over 1000 song types.

150.Sage_Thrasher.description: Smallest thrasher. Grayish-brown with yellow eyes and heavy spotting. Relies on sagebrush for nesting.

151.Black_capped_Vireo.description: Rare bird with a striking black hood and white spectacles. Endangered by habitat loss and cowbird parasitism.

152.Blue_headed_Vireo.description: Beautiful vireo with a blue-gray head, white spectacles, and greenish back. Very deliberate, slow movements.

153.Philadelphia_Vireo.description: Plain vireo, very similar to Warbling Vireo but usually shows more yellow on the underparts. Breeds in Canada.

154.Red_eyed_Vireo.description: A tireless singer even in the heat of midday. Olive-green above with a gray cap and red eye.

155.Warbling_Vireo.description: Plain gray-olive bird best known for its rambling, cheerful warble. Prefers treetops near water.

156.White_eyed_Vireo.description: Secretive bird of dense brush. 'Quick, with the beer check!' song. Pale eye and yellow spectacles.

157.Yellow_throated_Vireo.description: Bright yellow throat and breast with green back. 'Three-eight' song sounds like a hoarse Robin.

158.Bay_breasted_Warbler.description: Breeding males have a dark chestnut face, throat, and sides. Specialized on spruce budworms.

159.Black_and_white_Warbler.description: Striped like a zebra. Uniquely creeps along tree trunks and branches like a nuthatch.

160.Black_throated_Blue_Warbler.description: Males are elegant: midnight blue back, black face/throat, and pure white belly. 'Zoo-zoo-zoo-zee' song.

161.Blue_winged_Warbler.description: Yellow butterball with blue-gray wings. Song is a simple 'Bee-buzz'. Hybridizes with Golden-winged Warbler.

162.Canada_Warbler.description: Necklaced warbler. Blue-gray above, yellow below with a bold black necklace of streaks.

163.Cape_May_Warbler.description: Tiger-striped warbler with chestnut cheeks. High-pitched, seet-seet-seet song. Follows spruce budworm outbreaks.

164.Cerulean_Warbler.description: Sky-blue male lives high in the treetops. Declining rapidly due to fragmentation of mature forests.

165.Chestnut_sided_Warbler.description: Yellow cap and extensive chestnut streaks on sides. 'Pleased, pleased, pleased to MEETCHA' song.

166.Golden_winged_Warbler.description: Striking gray warbler with yellow wing patches and golden crown. Black throat and mask.

167.Hooded_Warbler.description: Bright yellow face surrounded by a black hood. Flashes white tail spots frequently.

168.Kentucky_Warbler.description: A bird of the forest floor with a black mask and yellow spectacles. Song is a rolling 'churry-churry-churry'.

169.Magnolia_Warbler.description: Black necklace on yellow breast, black mask, and white wing patches. Tail has a distinctive white band.

170.Mourning_Warbler.description: Skulking warbler with a gray hood and black patch on the breast (mourning veil). Avoids open view.

171.Myrtle_Warbler.description: The 'Butterbutt'. Abundant and hardy warbler with a bright yellow rump. Can digest wax on bayberries.

172.Nashville_Warbler.description: Small warbler with a gray head, white eye-ring, and yellow throat. Nests on the ground in moss.

173.Orange_crowned_Warbler.description: One of the drabber warblers. Olive-green overall with blurry streaks. The orange crown is rarely hidden.

174.Palm_Warbler.description: A tail-wagging ground warbler. Breeding adults have a rusty cap and yellow underparts.

175.Pine_Warbler.description: Strictly associated with pine trees. Large, heavy-billed warbler. Olive-green above, yellow below.

176.Prairie_Warbler.description: Tail-wagger of the brush. Yellow with black streaks on sides and a unique semi-circular black face pattern.

177.Prothonotary_Warbler.description: The 'Golden Swamp Warbler'. Brilliant whole-yellow head. Nests in tree cavities over water.

178.Swainson_Warbler.description: Drab brown, secretive warbler of the southeastern swamps. Famous for its loud, ringing song.

179.Tennessee_Warbler.description: Dainty warbler that resembles a vireo. Green back, gray head, and white eyebrow. loud staccato song.

180.Wilson_Warbler.description: Small, frantic yellow warbler with a distinct black cap (toupee). Often flycatches in low bushes.

181.Worm_eating_Warbler.description: Drab warbler with bold black stripes on a buffy head. Probes dead leaves for insect larvae (not earthworms).

182.Yellow_Warbler.description: Widespread sun-drop bird. Males have rusty streaks on the breast. 'Sweet, sweet, sweet, I'm so sweet!' song.

183.Northern_Waterthrush.description: Brown warbler that walks along water's edge constantly bobbing its tail. Creamy eyebrow.

184.Louisiana_Waterthrush.description: Similar to Northern Waterthrush but with a bright white eyebrow and unspotted throat. Prefers rushing water.

185.Bohemian_Waxwing.description: Large, gray-brown nomad of the north. Rusty undertail distinguish it from Cedar Waxwings.

186.Cedar_Waxwing.description: Silky, crested bird with waxy red tips on wing feathers. Highly social fruit-eaters.

187.American_Three_toed_Woodpecker.description: Specialized woodpecker that flakes bark off dead trees. Has a yellow crown patch and barred back.

188.Pileated_Woodpecker.description: Crow-sized woodpecker with a flaming red crest. Excavates large rectangular holes in search of carpenter ants.

189.Red_bellied_Woodpecker.description: Poorly named; the belly is barely red. Has a zebra-striped back and red nape/crown. Noisy 'churr' call.

190.Red_cockaded_Woodpecker.description: Endangered specialist of old-growth pines. Drills cavities in living trees infected with heart rot.

191.Red_headed_Woodpecker.description: Unmistakable with an entirely red head, black back, and large white wing patches. Catches insects in flight.

192.Downy_Woodpecker.description: The smallest North American woodpecker. Black and white styling. Short bill (unlike Hairy Woodpecker).

193.Bewick_Wren.description: Active wren with a long tail often flicked sideways. Bold white eyebrow. Declining in the East.

194.Cactus_Wren.description: Largest US wren. Heavily spotted breast. Nests in cholla cacti in the Sonoran desert.

195.Carolina_Wren.description: Large, rusty wren with a bold white eyebrow. Loud 'teakettle-teakettle-teakettle' song echoes in backyards.

196.House_Wren.description: Energetic, plain brown wren. Bubbling, exuberant song. Aggressively evicts other birds from nest boxes.

197.Marsh_Wren.description: Noisy denizen of the marshes. Rusty back with white stripes. Males build multiple 'dummy nests'.

198.Rock_Wren.description: Pale gray wren that bounces on rocks. Paves the entrance to its nest crevice with small stones.

199.Winter_Wren.description: Tiny, dark ball of energy with a stubby tail. Incredible, long, tinkling song for such a small bird.

200.Common_Yellowthroat.description: The 'masked bandit' warbler. Males have a black mask. Song is a distinctive 'witchety-witchety-witchety'.

Andean Tinamou.description: A ground-dwelling bird found in the Andes mountains. It has mottled plumage for camouflage.

Emu.description: The second-largest living bird by height. Endemic to Australia, it is flightless and has soft-feathered, brown plumage.

Common Ostrich.description: The largest living bird species. It is flightless and native to Africa, known for its speed and large eggs.

Southern Cassowary.description: A large, flightless bird with a distinctive helmet-like casque and vivid blue/red neck skin. Known as 'the world's most dangerous bird'.

Great Spotted Kiwi.description: The largest kiwi species. It is nocturnal, flightless, and has gray-brown mottled plumage.

Barred Tinamou.description: A shy, ground-dwelling bird of the Amazon rainforest.

Dusky-legged Guan.description: A large, turkey-like bird found in forests of Brazil and Argentina.

Ornate Tinamou.description: Inhabits the puna grasslands of the Andes.

Okarito Kiwi.description: A rare species of kiwi found only in the Okarito forest.

Black-billed Brushturkey.description: A mound-building bird typical of New Guinea forests.

Cinereous Tinamou.description: A smoky-gray tinamou found in the Amazon basin.

Greater Rhea.description: A large flightless bird of South America, resembling a small ostrich.

Tongan Megapode.description: A rare mound-builder endemic to Tonga, relying on volcanic heat for incubation.

Brushland Tinamou.description: Found in the Gran Chaco region of South America.

Darwins Nothura.description: A small tinamou of the Andean highlands.

Biak Scrubfowl.description: Endemic to the island of Biak in Indonesia.

Colombian Chachalaca.description: Endemic to Colombia, often seen in groups.

White-bellied Chachalaca.description: Found in Central America, known for its loud calls.

Northern Cassowary.description: A large cassowary of New Guinea with a single wattle.

Highland Tinamou.description: Inhabits montane forests in the Andes and Central America.

Red-winged Tinamou.description: Known for its rufous flight feathers visible in flight.

Black Tinamou.description: A rare and dark-plumaged tinamou of the Andes.

Southern Brown Kiwi.description: The most common kiwi species in New Zealand's South Island.

Cauca Guan.description: A rare guan found only in the Cauca Valley of Colombia.

Tawny-breasted Tinamou.description: Lives in high-elevation forests of the Andes.

Elegant Crested Tinamou.description: A beautiful tinamou with a long crest, found in Argentina.

White-browed Guan.description: Endemic to dry forests of northeastern Brazil.

Scaled Chachalaca.description: Endemic to Brazil, named for the scaled appearance of its breast feathers.

Little Tinamou.description: A small, widespread tinamou of Central and South America.

Plain Chachalaca.description: The only chachalaca found in the USA (Texas). Noisy and social.

Australian Brushturkey.description: A large mound-builder common in eastern Australia.

Andean Guan.description: Found in the high Andes, often seen running along branches.

North Island Brown Kiwi.description: Widespread in the North Island of NZ. Flightless and nocturnal.

Orange-footed Scrubfowl.description: Known for building massive incubation mounds of decaying vegetation.

Bearded Guan.description: A rare guan of Ecuador and Peru with a distinctive beard.

White-throated Tinamou.description: A rainforest tinamou with a white throat patch.

Dwarf Tinamou.description: A tiny, secretive tinamou of Brazilian grasslands.

Chilean Tinamou.description: Endemic to Chile, often hunted for sport.

Curve-billed Tinamou.description: Found in the páramo and puna of the Andes.

Black-fronted Piping Guan.description: A rare guan with a blue wattle and white wing patch.

White-crested Guan.description: Endemic to Brazil, known for its contrasting white crest.

Huayco Tinamou.description: Similar to the Red-winged Tinamou but found in the Bolivian Andes.

Chaco Chachalaca.description: Very common in the Gran Chaco region.

Marail Guan.description: Found in the Guiana Shield forests.

Crested Guan.description: A large guan of Central and northern South America.

Baudo Guan.description: Restricted to the Chocó region of Colombia/Ecuador.

Thicket Tinamou.description: Common in Mexico and Central American dry forests.

Great Tinamou.description: A large gamebird of Neotropical rainforests with a haunting song.

Lesser Nothura.description: A small, threatened tinamou of Brazil.

Blue-throated Piping Guan.description: A large bird with a blue wattle, found in the Amazon.

Rusty Tinamou.description: A small, reddish tinamou of Amazonia.

Somali Ostrich.description: Distinct from the Common Ostrich, with blue-grey skin.

Red-billed Brushturkey.description: A mound-builder with a red bill.

Patagonian Tinamou.description: Found in southern Chile and Argentina.

New Guinea Scrubfowl.description: A terrestrial bird of New Guinea.

Taczanowskis Tinamou.description: A rare tinamou of Peru and Bolivia.

Dwarf Cassowary.description: The smallest of the three cassowary species.

Maleo.description: Famous for laying its eggs in warm sand or volcanic soil, not mounds.

Quebracho Crested Tinamou.description: Found in the dry Chaco of Argentina and Paraguay.

Grey-legged Tinamou.description: Found in the northern Amazon/Orinoco region.

Moluccan Megapode.description: Roosts in trees but buries eggs in sand beaches at night.

Grey Tinamou.description: The largest tinamou species, bluish-grey in color.

Philippine Megapode.description: Common in the Philippines and Borneo.

Trinidad Piping Guan.description: One of the rarest birds in the world, endemic to Trinidad.

Small-billed Tinamou.description: Similar to the Tataupa Tinamou but with a shorter bill.

Chestnut-bellied Guan.description: Restricted to the Pantanal and Cerrado of Brazil.

Red-throated Piping Guan.description: Amazonian guan with a red throat wattle.

Bartletts Tinamou.description: Inhabits seasonally flooded forests in Amazonia.

White-bellied Nothura.description: Found in the Caatinga of Brazil and Bolivia.

Undulated Tinamou.description: Widespread and common in Amazonia/Cerrado. Characteristic 3-note call.

Spotted Nothura.description: Similar to a quail, very common in South American grasslands.

Tataupa Tinamou.description: Purple beak and legs; common in dry habitats.

Melanesian Megapode.description: Found in the Solomon Islands and Bismarck Archipelago.

Rufous-bellied Chachalaca.description: Note: Often confused with Chestnut-headed, differs in range/plumage.

Pale-browed Tinamou.description: Endemic to the Tumbesian region of Ecuador/Peru.

Choco Tinamou.description: Restricted to the Chocó of Colombia and Panama.

Brown Tinamou.description: A reddish-brown tinamou, common in its range.

Band-tailed Guan.description: Found in the mountains of Colombia and Venezuela.

Hooded Tinamou.description: Found in the Andes of Peru and Bolivia.

Rusty-margined Guan.description: Widespread in Brazil and adjacent countries.

Collared Brushturkey.description: A brush-turkey with a bare red neck collar.

Lesser Rhea.description: Smaller than the Greater Rhea, lives in high altitudes or Patagonia.

White-winged Guan.description: Rediscovered in 1977 in Peru after being thought extinct.

Tepui Tinamou.description: Restricted to the tepuis of Venezuela.

Berlepschs Tinamou.description: Similar to the Cinereous Tinamou, found in the Chocó.

Malleefowl.description: Famous for regulating its mound temperature with extreme precision.
